source.anchor: Original Samplinglib supplement: Finite sums preserve convergence in measure. Exact assumptions and formula below.
source.original_text:
On a finite measure space, take a finite family of sequences of almost-everywhere strongly measurable functions into a seminormed additive commutative group. If each sequence converges in measure to its given limit, the sums converge in measure to the sum of the limits.

The index set is finite and the sample measure is finite. The codomain is a seminormed additive commutative group.
Each term is almost-everywhere strongly measurable. Each sequence converges in measure to its given limit.

\left(F_{i,n}\xrightarrow{\mu} G_i\text{ for each }i\right)\ \Longrightarrow\ \sum_iF_{i,n}\xrightarrow{\mu}\sum_i G_i.

  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] {F : I → ℕ → Ω → E} {G : I → Ω → E}
  (hF : ∀ (i : I) (n : ℕ), MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (F i n) μ)
  (h : ∀ (i : I), MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (F i) Filter.atTop (G i)) :
  MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ (fun n ω => ∑ i, F i n ω) Filter.atTop fun ω => ∑ i, G i ω

blind_reconstruction.text:
Objects: F_i,n and G_i are E-valued functions on Omega, and the sums are finite over the whole index type I.

Domains: I finite; Omega measurable; mu finite; E a seminormed additive commutative group. F:I x N x Omega->E; G:I x Omega->E. No scalar field or vector-space structure is required.

Quantifiers: Universally I,Omega,E,instances,mu,F,G; assume for every i,n that F_i,n is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; assume for every i that F_i,n converges in mu-measure to G_i as n->infinity; then conclude the finite-sum convergence.

Assumptions: Every F_i,n is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. For each i separately, F_i,n -> G_i in mu-measure. No separate measurability assumption on G_i is written.

Conclusion: The functions omega->sum_i F_i,n(omega) converge in mu-measure, as n->infinity, to omega->sum_i G_i(omega).

Scopes: Convergence is in measure with respect to the fixed finite mu and the seminorm-induced pseudometric. The finite index set may be empty. No L^p or almost-sure convergence is asserted.

Constant dependencies: No constant or rate is specified; the same finite I is fixed throughout the limit.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.CountableConvergenceInMeasure
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.StronglyMeasurable.Basic

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.FiniteSumConvergenceInMeasure

open Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped BigOperators Topology
open CountableConvergenceInMeasure

/-- Finite sums of almost everywhere strongly measurable sequences
preserve convergence in measure on a finite measure space. -/
theorem tendstoInMeasure_fintype_sum
    {I Ω E : Type*} [Fintype I] [MeasurableSpace Ω] [SeminormedAddCommGroup E]
    {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {F : I → ℕ → Ω → E} {G : I → Ω → E}
    (hF : ∀ i n, AEStronglyMeasurable (F i n) μ)
    (h : ∀ i, TendstoInMeasure μ (F i) atTop (G i)) :
    TendstoInMeasure μ (fun n ω => ∑ i, F i n ω) atTop (fun ω => ∑ i, G i ω) := by
  have hm (n : ℕ) : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ω => ∑ i, F i n ω) μ := by
    exact (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hF i n)).congr
      (Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by simp only [Finset.sum_apply])
  refine (exists_seq_tendstoInMeasure_atTop_iff hm).2 ?_
  intro n hn
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hPath⟩ := exists_seq_tendsto_ae_of_countable
    (fun i => (h i).comp hn.tendsto_atTop)
  refine ⟨k, hk, ?_⟩
  filter_upwards [hPath] with ω hω
  exact tendsto_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hω i)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.FiniteSumConvergenceInMeasure

steps.title: Use one subsequence for the whole family
steps.text: Start from any subsequence and choose a single further subsequence on which all component limits hold almost everywhere.
steps.formula: F_{i,n_{k_\ell}}(\omega)\to G_i(\omega)\qquad\text{for every }i\text{ on one full-measure event}.
steps.lean:
have hm (n : ℕ) : AEStronglyMeasurable (fun ω => ∑ i, F i n ω) μ := by
    exact (Finset.aestronglyMeasurable_sum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hF i n)).congr
      (Eventually.of_forall fun ω => by simp only [Finset.sum_apply])
  refine (exists_seq_tendstoInMeasure_atTop_iff hm).2 ?_
  intro n hn
  obtain ⟨k, hk, hPath⟩ := exists_seq_tendsto_ae_of_countable
    (fun i => (h i).comp hn.tendsto_atTop)
  refine ⟨k, hk, ?_⟩

steps.title: Sum the limits
steps.text: Continuity of finite addition gives the sum limit on that event. The finite sums are almost-everywhere strongly measurable, so the subsequence criterion gives convergence in measure.
steps.lean:
filter_upwards [hPath] with ω hω
  exact tendsto_finsetSum Finset.univ (fun i _ => hω i)

lesson.lean_proof: Use the existing common subsequence theorem and preserve the resulting almost-everywhere limits under addition.
